label: contrasting two alternatives negatively (X se nahin, Y se)
note: Introduced by HI-C94-se-nahiin, with the one new noun tren supplied by HI-C94-train. The note was EXACTLY RIGHT that the frame needs se, and se was taught in chapter 98 -- and bas se with it, so mock 2 reading item 13 (main bas se nahiin, tren se jaaungaa) cost a single word. Two things are worth drilling. First, EACH OPTION KEEPS ITS OWN se: English drops the second by, Hindi does not, so counting the se tells a reader whether a swap is being offered. Second, the POSITION of nahiin says how much is being denied -- in front of the verb it denies the whole sentence, after a noun-plus-postposition it denies only that phrase -- and an item asking how the speaker will travel is answered by the phrase AFTER the negative, which is why the paper prints the rejected option first.
